tasks.title: Add graph navigation and reverse code-to-rationale inspection
tasks.description:
Outcome: Supervisor graph navigation and reverse source-to-rationale inspection.

Current implementation: The Web UI already organizes project entities; graph/code/rationale exploration is planned rather than a replacement planner.

Implementation responsibility:
- Implement the reviewed prototype design using suitable React/router infrastructure to navigate project, feature, phase, task, code area, decision and verification evidence.
- Show selected workspace/revision and edge provenance, unknown/stale/review state and relevant prior tasks.
- Provide inspectable paths/impact with bounded server queries and deep links to actual source/historical content.
- Keep human-supervisor and agent permissions distinct; graph interactions do not silently mutate canonical decisions or task order.

Acceptance and evidence:
- A user can inspect which tasks changed a code area and why, including unrelated task history.
- Navigation preserves project/source context and supports explicit continuation.
- No hidden source relink or decision promotion occurs on selecting a graph node.

- packages/plan-server/src/serve.ts:1 (module entry; inspect the current owning functions before editing).
- packages/plan-core/src/api-v1.ts:1 (module entry; inspect the current owning functions before editing).

Navigation paths are dated evidence at the inspected checkout, not permanent code identity. Read current source precedents, Project Guidelines and canonical Accepted Decisions before implementation. Preserve entity IDs/history, phase-scoped handoffs, atomic ownership, explicit recovery and derived parent state. Use isolated fixtures and bounded verification.

Detailed target: docs/agent-brain/architecture.md; the execution map is .planner/docs/agent-brain-plan.md. This contract replaces the old accumulated task text. No implementation, real migration, dashboard, Git publication or release is performed by planning.

UI design and domain boundary: Implement the new Web UI from the reviewed prototype canvases; the current UI appearance is not the target. Read docs/agent-brain/ui-prototypes.md and confirm the applicable design revision before visual implementation. Reuse suitable typed React/router/accessibility infrastructure. Core/service APIs own eligibility, priority, permissions, relationships and evidence interpretation; the UI renders their results, submits commands and manages presentation/drafts. Prototype fixtures are illustrative, never a live backend or a competing source of domain policy.

tasks.title: Expose setup, context analysis and review state in supervisor workflows
tasks.description:
Outcome: Supervisor setup, context and review controls that remain useful without Heca.

Current implementation: Sketches imply controls but do not prove provider, execution or collaboration availability.

Implementation responsibility:
- Expose provider/setup capability coverage and relevant context/preparation state from real service results.
- Show required review obligations, applicable standards, evidence and verification gaps with clear current/historical scope.
- Keep action availability tied to the owning service/principal; display explicit unavailable/incompatible/denied states.
- Integrate compact impact/receipt results and avoid full-plan reloads or model calls for routine synchronization.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Resume/planner/graph/code/recorded checks work with no Heca connection.
- A checked item or old passing test does not appear as current conformity proof.
- UI actions have an implemented owner and honest outcomes rather than mock success.
